# Intake Brief — Incremental sync: only export/push changed work items instead of full JSONL (WL-0MSAKUBKW006FN8Q)

## Problem statement

Every `wl sync` fully re-exports the entire SQLite database to JSONL (**11.6 MB, 2133 work items, 7494 comments**) and re-pushes the whole file to `refs/worklog/data` via a temp worktree — even when only a handful of items changed. This full-rewrite-per-sync makes syncs take 5–19 s (measured) and is the root cause of the pane timeout issue in WL-0MSAKM838006RZNR. `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` already lists "Incremental sync: Only sync changed items" as a planned enhancement.

## Users

- **Anyone running `wl sync`** (agents, operators, TUI panes) on large worklog datasets — syncs become faster and less disruptive, and the Herdr 10 s timeout problem (WL-0MSAKM838006RZNR) stops recurring without needing constant timeout tuning.
- **Teams sharing a canonical worklog ref** — fewer full-file rewrites means less churn on the shared ref and faster pulls/pushes.

User story: *As an operator, when only a few work items changed since my last sync, I want `wl sync` to export and push only those changes, so a typical sync takes seconds instead of 10+ seconds and no longer trips client timeouts.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After an initial full sync, a sync that changes a small set of items (e.g., ≤ 5 items/comments) performs the local export and git push without rewriting the full 11.6 MB JSONL file (measured: local export bytes written and `git add` payload are proportional to the changed records, not the dataset size).
- [ ] Typical incremental sync completes in ≤ 3 s on the current dataset (2133 items / 7494 comments) for small change sets (baseline today: full sync ~5.8 s local, 5–19 s with network variance).
- [ ] Correctness is preserved: after an incremental push and a subsequent full pull, local and remote data converge (same items/comments/edges/audits as today, verified by the existing sync test suite + a convergence test that interleaves incremental and full syncs).
- [ ] Deletions propagate: soft-deleted items (`status: 'deleted'`) are included in deltas so remote copies converge.
- [ ] Full-snapshot fallback works: first sync, sync after an interrupted/corrupt delta chain, and any sync where the delta cannot be applied cleanly fall back to the current full export/merge path with no data loss.
- [ ] Backward compatibility: the shared `refs/worklog/data` ref remains readable by existing clients (older `wl` versions, Herdr, Pi TUI extension); any format change is additive and documented, or gated behind a sync-state marker with automatic fallback.
- [ ] Unit/integration tests added for the dirty-tracking, delta export/merge, deletion propagation, and fallback paths; full project test suite passes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded**; it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- The shared ref and existing readers must not break: any format change requires backward compatibility or a documented migration with automatic full-snapshot fallback.
- Do not regress the concurrency protections: the file lock, single-flight guard, and `--if-idle` skip semantics (WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E) must continue to work with the incremental path.
- Keep the merge semantics: field-level conflict resolution by ID + timestamp (`mergeWorkItems`, `mergeComments`, `mergeDependencyEdges`, `mergeAuditResults` in `src/sync.ts`) is the correctness backbone — deltas must feed through the same resolution logic.
- Note: git already delta-compresses the network payload of a push, so the main wins are local (full export write, temp-worktree file copy, `git add` hashing/compressing of 11.6 MB, pull-side `git show` + parse). The design should target those costs.
- This is a design-heavy optimization: the implementing agent should pick an approach during planning (options below); the ACs are behavior-level.

## Existing state

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `exportForSync()` exports **all** work items, comments, dependency edges, and audit results via `jsonlSvc.exportToJsonlAsync()` to the JSONL path; `deleteLocalJsonl()` removes it after a successful push (ephemeral pattern).
- `src/jsonl.ts` — `buildJsonlContent()` emits a flat, sorted set of records (`type: workitem | comment | audit_result`) plus dependencies derived from edges. `importFromJsonlContent()` parses the same format. No version/header metadata; a delta file of the same record types is a valid subset of the format.
- `src/commands/sync.ts` / `src/sync.ts` — pull path: `git fetch` + streamed `git show` of the remote JSONL (`execGitCaptureStdout`), parse, then by-ID merge (`mergeWorkItems`/`mergeComments`/`mergeDependencyEdges`/`mergeAuditResults`); push path: `gitPushDataFileToBranch` builds a temp worktree, copies the full JSONL, commits, pushes `HEAD:refs/worklog/data`.
- Deletions are soft (`status: 'deleted'`), so records persist in the JSONL — no hard-delete tombstone format is needed for deltas.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §"Future Considerations" lists: (1) Incremental sync: only sync changed items, (2) Background sync, (3) Compression, (4) Delta encoding.
- No per-item dirty tracking exists today; there is a `last-sync-time` file written after successful syncs (`src/commands/sync.ts`).

## Desired change (approach options — decide in planning)

1. **Dirty tracking + delta export (preferred direction):** add per-record change tracking (e.g., an `updatedAt` threshold from the previous successful export, or a dirty set in SQLite). On sync, export only records changed since the last export to the JSONL and push that delta; readers (this codebase only — Herdr and the Pi TUI extension call the `wl` CLI, not the JSONL directly) apply deltas over the last full snapshot. Periodic full snapshots (e.g., every N syncs or when the delta log exceeds a size threshold) bound replay cost; automatic full-snapshot fallback on first sync / mismatch / corruption.
2. **Batched full rewrites:** keep the full-file format but only export+push when accumulated changes cross a threshold (fewer, bigger syncs). Simplest, backward-compatible, but does not reduce per-sync cost when a push happens — lower value than option 1; acceptable if option 1 proves too invasive.
3. **Sharded JSONL:** split records across shard files on the ref so only changed shards are rewritten. Compatible but adds ref/file management complexity.

Recommended: option 1 with a full-snapshot fallback, keeping the by-ID merge as the correctness backbone.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — dirty-tracking state, `exportForSync()` changed to delta-aware export (full vs. delta).
- `src/jsonl.ts` — optional record header/version metadata, delta assembly (unchanged record types), full-snapshot fallback support.
- `src/commands/sync.ts` — sync orchestration: decide full vs. incremental, apply deltas on the pull side, schedule periodic full snapshots.
- `src/sync.ts` — merge entry points to accept delta records and detect when a full snapshot is required (missing base, chain mismatch).
- `tests/` — new tests for dirty tracking, delta export/merge, deletion propagation, convergence, fallback.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — update the "Incremental sync" future-consideration entry to reflect the implemented design.

## Related work

- **wl sync timeouts: 10s Herdr auto-sync safety timeout kills legitimate slow syncs (WL-0MSAKM838006RZNR, open, intake_complete)** — the item this was discovered from (`discovered-from:WL-0MSAKM838006RZNR`); its ACs include making syncs fast enough not to trip client timeouts.
- **wl sync lock storm: 60+ stuck sync processes (WL-0MSAB7ZUC004SK7E, completed)** — concurrency guards (`--if-idle`, single-flight, file lock) that must keep working.
- **Add exponential back-off to file lock retry (WL-0MM0BT1FA0X23LTN, completed)** — lock contention behavior relevant to sync timing.
- **Remove autoExport: SQLite as single source of truth with ephemeral JSONL (WL-0MN53C1BZ17WJRBR, completed)** — established the ephemeral JSONL pattern this item extends.
- **docs/ARCHITECTURE.md** — "Future Considerations" § lists incremental sync as planned.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** Herdr and the Pi TUI extension read worklog data via the `wl` CLI (verified: they invoke `wl` subprocesses), so only the worklog codebase itself reads the JSONL — a delta format change is tractable if older `wl` versions on other machines are considered.
- **Risk:** incremental formats can silently diverge (missed updates, orphaned records, replay gaps). Mitigation: by-ID merge remains the resolution backbone, deltas feed through it, full-snapshot fallback on any uncertainty, and a convergence test that interleaves incremental and full syncs.
- **Risk:** dirty tracking can miss changes if writes bypass the tracking layer (direct DB writes, imports, migrations). Mitigation: track at the export boundary using `updatedAt` thresholds rather than write interception, and treat "no known baseline" as full export.
- **Risk:** periodic full snapshots add occasional slow syncs; threshold tuning (count/time/size) needed. Keep the threshold conservative.
- **Scope-creep guard:** background async sync, JSONL compression, and delta encoding of the git transport are separate items listed in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`; record as linked work items rather than folding into this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should we create the incremental sync follow-up work item?" — Answer (operator): "yes create that". Source: interactive reply following the WL-0MSAKM838006RZNR intake.
- OPEN QUESTION (for planning): choose between approach options 1 (delta export), 2 (batched full rewrites), and 3 (sharded JSONL) — brief recommends option 1 with full-snapshot fallback; ACs are behavior-level and approach-agnostic.
- OPEN QUESTION (for planning): acceptable full-snapshot cadence (every N syncs / time-based / delta-size threshold) — to be determined during planning; ACs only require that typical incremental syncs are small and fast.

# Heartbeat: Surface Audit Progress and Completion Notifications

## Problem statement

The heartbeat skill runs audits headlessly via `pi -p --mode json --no-session /skill:audit <id>` when the completed/in_review queue reaches 10+ items. From the producer's perspective this work is invisible: there is no live view, no progress signal, and no notification when the audit completes. The audit either lands silently or fails silently (timeout/error) — see the evaluation of Pi subprocess mechanisms (discovered-from:WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7), which identified this as the main visibility gap of headless pi usage.

## Users

- **Producers / operators** — want to know when a background heartbeat audit starts, is running, and finishes (with its verdict), so they can review results without polling the worklog.

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when the heartbeat starts an audit, I want to see a notification so I know background work is happening."
- "As a producer, when a heartbeat audit completes, I want the result (Ready to close: Yes/No) surfaced so I don't have to discover it by chance."
- "As a producer, when a heartbeat audit fails or times out, I want that surfaced too, with the reason."

## Expected behaviour

- On heartbeat audit start: surface a notification (e.g. herdr toast and/or a work-item comment).
- On completion: surface the verdict ('Ready to close: Yes/No') — e.g. via toast, work-item comment, or both.
- On failure/timeout: surface the failure reason.

## Suggested implementation approach

- Extend the heartbeat skill (`.pi/skills/heartbeat/SKILL.md` and `scripts/heartbeat.py`) to emit notifications around the `pi -p` audit invocation.
- Reuse existing notification plumbing where available (herdr `notification show` used by the worklist plugin's `notify.ts`; `wl comment add` for a durable record on the audited item).
- Consider an opt-out flag/env var so automated environments (cron, CI) can suppress noisy notifications.

## Acceptance criteria

1. When the heartbeat dispatches an audit, a visible start notification is produced.
2. When the audit completes, the verdict ('Ready to close: Yes/No') is surfaced via a notification and/or a comment on the work item.
3. When the audit fails or times out, the failure is surfaced with the reason.
4. Notifications are non-blocking (heartbeat continues to exit 0 on success) and can be suppressed for unattended environments.
5. Existing heartbeat tests still pass; new tests cover start/completion/failure notification paths.
6. All related documentation (SKILL.md) is updated to reflect the changes.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
data.title: Heartbeat: surface audit progress and completion notifications

# Hybrid Pi Dispatch: Pane When in a Herdr Session, Headless Fallback Otherwise

## Problem statement

The evaluation of Pi subprocess mechanisms (discovered-from:WL-0MSG4VSP10020NL7) found that /skill:audit is dispatched two ways: user-initiated audits open a visible herdr pi pane via send-to-pi.sh, while automated contexts (heartbeat, cron, CI, ssh) must run headless via `pi -p --mode json`. Currently the choice of mechanism is hard-wired per caller and there is no shared way to get a visible pane when a herdr session exists and fall back to a headless subprocess when it does not. The podcast editor (open_source_llm/experimental/herdr-podcast-editor) already implements exactly this hybrid pattern via a HERDR_ENV check; it is a proven precedent to generalise.

## Users

- **Producers / operators** — want agent work to be visible whenever a herdr session is present, even when the invocation originates from a script or automated context.
- **Skills authors / plugin authors** — want a single reusable dispatch primitive instead of maintaining two mechanisms.

Example user stories:

- "As a producer, when an audit is triggered from a context that has a herdr session available, I want it to open in a visible pi pane so I can watch it."
- "As a producer, when no herdr session is available, I want the same invocation to fall back to headless execution so the work still happens."
- "As a plugin author, I want to dispatch a skill to pi once and have it choose pane-vs-headless automatically."

## Expected behaviour

- A shared dispatch helper determines at runtime whether a herdr session/pane environment is available (e.g. HERDR_ENV or herdr CLI/socket presence, mirroring the podcast editor).
- When available: dispatch via send-to-pi.sh (visible pane).
- When unavailable: fall back to `pi -p --mode json` headless execution with the same command.
- Existing callers keep their behaviour; new callers (e.g. heartbeat audits, user-initiated audits outside the worklist) opt in.

## Suggested implementation approach

- Add the helper to the shared herdr scripts (packages/herdr/shared/) and/or a small skill-level utility so both herdr code and skills can use it.
- Model the fallback on the podcast editor's send-to-pi.sh wrapper + direct-subprocess branch.
- Wire the heartbeat audit dispatch to use the hybrid helper (pane when herdr present, headless otherwise), which also delivers visibility (see WL-0MSG5THFC004WJEI).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A shared dispatch helper exists that selects pane vs headless at runtime based on herdr availability.
2. With a herdr environment present, dispatch opens a visible pi pane running the given command.
3. Without a herdr environment, dispatch runs the command headless via `pi -p --mode json` and returns programmatic output.
4. At least one existing caller (e.g. heartbeat audit dispatch) is converted to use the helper without regressing its current behaviour.
5. Tests cover both branches (herdr present / absent).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
data.title: Hybrid pi dispatch: pane when in a herdr session, headless fallback otherwise

## Problem

During the excessive-spawn investigation (WL-0MSB19J56006E87J) and in normal operation, `worklog.db-wal` grows large under concurrent writer load (16MB WAL observed). Worklog uses SQLite in WAL mode by design (`src/persistent-store.ts` sets `journal_mode = WAL` for concurrency).

Observations:

- Writes land in `worklog.db-wal` first; `worklog.db` mtime/size stays unchanged until a checkpoint merges the WAL back. A 66KB `worklog.db-wal` was observed in `open_source_llm/.worklog` while `worklog.db` sat untouched — and the WAL files disappear once all processes close (checkpoint on close / auto-checkpoint).
- Under the spawn storm (206 concurrent wl processes), the WAL reached ~16MB, meaning auto-checkpointing was not keeping up with write volume.

Why this matters:

1. **Read cost:** SQLite reads must scan the WAL, so a large WAL slows every read query.
2. **Cache invalidation:** mtime/size of `worklog.db` alone is unreliable while a large WAL holds live writes (see WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3 AC #2 — cache must be WAL-aware).
3. **Crash/recovery:** a large WAL means longer recovery time on abnormal exit.

## Goals

- Understand current checkpointing behavior: default auto-checkpoint threshold, when/where wl checkpoints (per-write? on close? explicit wal_checkpoint?), and how concurrent writers interact.
- Determine whether a large-WAL state is a correctness risk or only a performance cost.
- Decide if wl should checkpoint after write batches (e.g., after `wl sync` or bulk mutations) or rely on auto-checkpoint.

## Suggested approach

- Inspect `src/persistent-store.ts` and `src/database.ts` for pragma settings and any checkpoint logic.
- Reproduce: run N concurrent write processes against one worklog and measure WAL growth, read latency, and checkpoint behavior.
- Consider adding an explicit `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE/TRUNCATE)` after write-heavy operations if evidence supports it.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Documented understanding of when/where checkpointing happens and why a 16MB WAL occurred (root cause identified, reproduced, or ruled out).
2. Measured impact of large WAL on read latency (before/after numbers).
3. A recommendation recorded on this item: leave as-is, add explicit checkpointing, or tune auto-checkpoint threshold — with rationale and risk notes.
4. Any code change is tested and does not regress the full test suite.

# Herdr selection list: no indication of items below the fold

## Problem statement

When the herdr worklist selection list (`createListRenderer` in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`) has more work items than fit in the visible list area, the renderer silently trims the visible window to fit the pane height. There is no visual cue (scroll marker, count, ellipsis) that additional items exist below the fold, so users cannot tell the list is truncated and may miss items.

## Users

Anyone using the herdr worklist pane (`worklog-selection-list` plug) to browse/select work items, in particular with more items than fit on screen (the default list of 20+ items on smaller panes, or with the metadata panel reserving 20–40% of the height).

User story: *"As a herdr user, when the worklist pane shows more items than fit, I want to see a `▼ more` marker so I know the list continues below the fold and I can scroll (j/k) to see the rest."*

User story: *"As a herdr user who has scrolled down, I want to see an `▲ more` marker at the top of the list so I know there are items above the current viewport."*

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the flattened item list exceeds the visible list area at scroll offset 0, the rendered list output contains a dim-styled `▼ more` marker at the bottom of the items region (after the last visible item, before the footer/fill rows).
- When the list is scrolled down (scrollOffset > 0) with items above the viewport, the rendered output contains a dim-styled `▲ more` marker at the top of the items region (before the first visible item/group separator).
- When all items fit in the visible area (no overflow, scrollOffset = 0), no indicators are rendered.
- The `rows - 1` line-count invariant is preserved with indicators active: rendered output plus the notification line still fits the pane height (regression guard for WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO).
- Indicators are non-selectable display-only rows: they do not consume navigation state, selection index, or hierarchy scroll offset (`getVisibleItems`, `_adjustScroll` semantics unchanged).
- New unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` cover: indicator shown when items exist below the fold; `▲ more` shown when scrolled; no indicators when the list fits; line-count invariant with indicators active.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline. Implementing agents should not manually update CHANGELOG.md.

## Constraints

- Must preserve the `rows - 1` line-count invariant established in WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO (notification line always fits; header never scrolls off the top).
- Indicator wording is generic ("more"), not exact counts — group separator rows make exact "N more" counts unreliable.
- Scope is list mode only: the detail view and the metadata panel (WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X) are unchanged.
- Match existing styling conventions: dim-styled (`ANSI.dim`), consistent with other non-interactive chrome (footer hints, filter bar).
- Indicator rows must be included in the render budget (the `visible` trimming loop and the fill-blank count) so output never exceeds the pane.

## Existing state

- `createListRenderer` sizes the visible window with `flatItems.slice(scrollOffset, scrollOffset + listHeight)` and trims it with `visible.slice(0, -1)` when items + group separators exceed `budgetForItemsAndSeps`. Nothing signals that trimming happened.
- The pane header shows `(top N of M)` only when the *fetch* was truncated (`totalCount > items.length`), not when the *display* is truncated by the viewport — so a full fetch with a small pane shows no cue at all.
- Scrolling works (j/k via `scrollOffset`, `_adjustScroll` keeps the selection visible), but at rest positions there is no indication of hidden items in either direction.
- The Pi TUI browse list (`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.ts`) is a separate surface and already shows `(top N of M)` in its title; pi's built-in `SelectList` component renders a `(N/M)` scroll-info line when overflow exists — the established pattern this change mirrors.

## Desired change

- In `createListRenderer` (list mode), after the visible window is trimmed to fit:
  - Emit a dim `▼ more` line at the bottom of the items region when `scrollOffset + visible.length < flatItems.length` (items below the fold).
  - Emit a dim `▲ more` line at the top of the items region when `scrollOffset > 0` (items above the viewport).
  - Account for indicator rows in the budget: include them in the trimming calculation and in the fill-blank `used` count so the `rows - 1` invariant holds.
  - Edge case: if reserving the bottom indicator row trims the window so that `scrollOffset + visible.length == flatItems.length`, the bottom indicator is omitted (the list then fully fits); this must terminate in a single pass (no loop).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `createListRenderer`: compute indicator presence from `scrollOffset`/the trimmed visible window, emit `▼ more`/`▲ more` rows, and include them in the budget (`budgetForItemsAndSeps` trimming loop + fill-blank `used` count).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — add unit tests: indicator shown when items below fold; `▲ more` shown when scrolled; no indicators when list fits; line-count invariant with indicators active; indicators are non-selectable display rows.

## Related work

- [Herdr plugin: selection list header and top lines cut off top of pane (WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO)] — completed; established the `rows - 1` line-count invariant and the visible-window trimming logic this change extends.
- [Herdr plugin: reserve bottom 40% of selection list for item metadata and last command (WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X)] — completed; defines `listArea`/`panelHeight`, the fold boundary of the list region.
- [Create a work item selection list in Herdr (WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP)] — origin of the selection list.
- pi-tui `SelectList` component (`node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-tui/dist/components/select-list.js`) — reference pattern: `(N/M)` scroll-info line when the list overflows `maxVisible`.

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumption: generic "more" wording is sufficient (user: "more" is fine); exact counts are intentionally avoided because group separators make them unreliable.
- Risk: indicator rows shrink the visible item window by up to 2 rows when overflow exists. Acceptable — the alternative (no indicator) is the bug being fixed.
- Risk: budget accounting bugs could regress the WL-0MSAAON63003N6LO line-count invariant. Mitigation: the existing invariant tests plus new tests with indicators active cover both top and bottom indicators.
- Edge case: bottom indicator row reservation could trim the window to fully fit, making the indicator unnecessary — handle without looping.
- Scope-creep guard: the Pi TUI browse list also lacks a fold indicator, but it already shows `(top N of M)`; improving that surface is out of scope and could be tracked as a separate work item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Indicator style — which do you prefer? (a) a footer line in the items region like `▼ N more` (dim), shown when items exist below the fold; (b) a position indicator like `(N/M)`; (c) both: `▼ N more` footer plus a `▲ N more` header when scrolled down" — Answer (user): "(c) Both". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Scope — should this cover only the list-mode pane (herdr worklist), or also the detail-view scroll indicator (which already exists via the metadata panel scroll)?" — Answer (user): "confirm" (list-mode only). Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Count precision — exact remaining count (e.g. `▼ 5 more`) vs. a generic marker (e.g. `▼ more`)? Exact counts can be wrong when group separators consume rows." — Answer (user): "`more` is fine". Source: interactive reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MP15YJEQ000FVWS** – Documentation: colour mapping & fallbacks (completed)
- **WL-0MLRFF0771A8NAVW** – TUI: prevent mouse click-through from dialogs to underlying widgets (completed)
- **WL-0MLOS7X1C1P82B5J** – Append no-questions instruction to OpenCode prompt (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-herdr-below-fold-indicator-WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ.md` — matched: additional, area, cannot, count, createlistrenderer, exist, fit, fold, height, herdr, indication, indicator, items, list, marker, packages, pane, renderer, scroll, selection, silently, src, tell, there, trims, truncated, users, visible, visual, when, window, work, worklist
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-WL-0MSDZ64J8005Q2JJ-grid-rebalance-python-tests-mocked-socke/packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: additional, area, cannot, count, exist, height, herdr, indicator, items, list, marker, packages, pane, renderer, scroll, selection, silently, src, tell, there, visible, when, work, worklist
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: additional, area, cannot, count, exist, height, herdr, indicator, items, list, marker, packages, pane, renderer, scroll, selection, silently, src, tell, there, visible, when, work, worklist

# Herdr worklist: mouse and touch support in the selection list (WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ)

## Problem statement

The Herdr work item selection list (`packages/herdr` TUI) is keyboard-only. Users of Herdr — a mouse-first, terminal workspace manager — cannot click or tap a work item to select it, cannot use the mouse wheel or touch gestures to scroll the list, and the detail/filter views are unreachable without keys. This makes the selection list feel foreign inside Herdr's pointer-friendly environment and unusable on touch-first devices (tablets, touch laptops).

## Users

- **Herdr users** who expect a pointer-driven experience: click/tap to pick an item, wheel/touch-scroll to browse.
- **Touch-device users** (tablets, touch laptops, convertible terminals) who have no usable keyboard navigation path — touch taps and drags must work.
- **Human reviewers/auditors** who switch between many work items quickly and want to point at a row instead of counting keystrokes.

### User stories

- As a Herdr user, I want to click or tap a row in the work item list so the selection moves to that item.
- As a Herdr user, I want to double-click or double-tap an item so it opens in the detail view (same as pressing Enter).
- As a Herdr user, I want to scroll the mouse wheel (or a two-finger touch scroll) in the list so the selection moves up/down like the arrow keys.
- As a Herdr user, I want to scroll the wheel in the detail view so the description scrolls without using keys.
- As a Herdr user, I want to tap a stage option in the filter prompt so the filter is applied without typing digits.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Mouse tracking is enabled/disabled with the TUI lifecycle**: entering raw mode emits the mouse-tracking enable sequences (`\x1b[?1000h\x1b[?1002h\x1b[?1006h` — button-event tracking + SGR extended coordinates); cleanup/exit emits the matching disable sequences. Verified by test (sequence strings are emitted on setup/cleanup) and manual smoke-run.
2. **Click/tap selects a row**: a single left click/tap on a visible list row moves the selection to that item (equivalent of the up/down arrow keys). Verified by unit tests on the row-mapping + dispatch logic.
3. **Double-click/tap opens details**: two clicks within the double-click window on the same row activate that item (equivalent of Enter), including from the detail view back to the list. Verified by unit test.
4. **Wheel and touch-scroll navigate**: wheel-up/wheel-down (buttons 64/65) and equivalent touch scrolls move the selection in list mode and scroll the detail content in detail mode (page/line scroll consistent with keyboard `j`/`k`). Verified by unit test.
5. **Filter prompt is pointer-sensitive**: tapping a stage option row in the filter prompt applies that stage filter (equivalent of pressing the digit key). Verified by unit test.
6. **Keyboard navigation is unaffected**: all existing key sequences still behave as before; unparsable/unknown mouse sequences are ignored without crashing or corrupting state. Existing `handleKeypress` tests continue to pass.
7. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant docs site entries (e.g., docs/dev/ input-handling notes).
8. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Mouse support is **additive** — existing keyboard navigation (arrows, `j`/`k`, Enter, Escape, chords) must keep working unchanged.
- Must work through the terminal's standard mouse-reporting protocol: SGR mouse events (`\x1b[<b;x;yM` press / `\x1b[<b;x;y m` release), with coordinates 1-based. Touch events arrive translated as mouse events (tap = left click, drag = motion, two-finger scroll = wheel) in terminals that support it — the plugin must not require any terminal-specific feature beyond SGR reporting (widely supported: xterm, tmux, kitty, wezterm, iTerm2, Windows Terminal).
- Drag-motion events (button code with the 32 motion bit) must not cause accidental selection jumps; motion is either used for an explicit touch-drag scroll or ignored safely.
- Mouse sequences arrive as raw stdin chunks (e.g. `\x1b[<0;10;5M`); they must be detected and consumed before the existing keypress parser sees them, and must not be mistaken for arrow-key escape sequences.
- The pane-hidden pause logic (pause-when-hidden) is out of scope — input is not read while the pane is hidden anyway.
- Fallback: terminals without mouse reporting simply never send mouse events; the list remains fully keyboard-usable (fail-soft).

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (2790 lines) is the selection-list TUI: `runWorklistTui` sets raw mode (`process.stdin.setRawMode(true)`), reads input via `process.stdin.on('data', onData)`, and dispatches through `handleKeypress(state, key, termSize)` → `keyToAction(key)`.
- No mouse-tracking escape sequences are emitted; no SGR mouse events are parsed. Unknown sequences currently fall through `keyToAction` to `default → null`.
- `ANSI` constants object (line 132) already holds terminal escapes — the natural home for mouse enable/disable sequences.
- Rendering computes row geometry in `createListRenderer`: a header row at the top, the list area (`listArea = rows - 1 - panelHeight`), a notification row, and a metadata panel at the bottom. Detail mode renders a `formatDetailView` block; filter mode renders `formatFilterPrompt` with digit-key stage options.
- Tests live in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (vitest); `handleKeypress` is a pure function tested directly — the new mouse logic should follow the same pattern (pure, unit-testable).

## Desired change

1. Add ANSI constants for mouse tracking enable (`\x1b[?1000h\x1b[?1002h\x1b[?1006h`) and disable (`\x1b[?1000l\x1b[?1002l\x1b[?1006l`).
2. In `runWorklistTui`, emit enable sequences when entering raw mode and disable sequences in `cleanup()`.
3. Add a pure `parseMouseEvent(key: string)` helper that recognizes `\x1b[<...M`/`\x1b[<...m` and returns `{ button, x, y, release } | null`.
4. Add a pure row-mapping helper that converts a click's 1-based `y` into a list row (accounting for the header offset and `scrollOffset`), a detail-view scroll position, or a filter-prompt option, depending on `state.mode`.
5. Add `mapMouseToAction(state, mouseEvent, termSize)` returning an action (`select-row`, `open-detail`, `wheel-up/down`, `scroll-detail`, `filter-stage`, etc.) and dispatch it from `onData` before the keypress path; track last-click time/position for double-click detection (~400 ms window).
6. Add unit tests mirroring the existing `handleKeypress` suite: parser, row mapping per mode, wheel dispatch, double-click window, filter-tap, and "unknown mouse sequence is ignored" regression.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — mouse enable/disable sequences, SGR event parser, row→item mapping, mouse dispatch in `onData`, double-click detection (primary change).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — unit tests for the parser, per-mode mapping, wheel/double-click/filter-tap dispatch, and unknown-sequence regression.
- `packages/herdr/dist/` — rebuilt artifacts via `npm run build` (tsc), kept in sync with source.
- `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` — documents the input/refresh loop; add a note about mouse input if behavior interacts with it (minor).

## Related work

- `Create a work item selection list in Herdr (WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP)` — the parent feature that built this list; its AC #5 defined keyboard navigation, this item extends input to pointers.
- `Impl: visibility-gated auto-refresh/sync in worklist TUI (WL-0MSB4473J004NYO5)` — owns the input loop/timers this change touches (input is only read while the pane is visible).
- `Mouse click on Work Items tree does not update details (WL-0MLAJ3Z750G25EJE)` — historical pointer bug in the older Pi TUI; the click-select behavior contract should match (click selects, details follow).
- `Critical: TUI closes when clicking anywhere (WL-0MKX2C2X007IRR8G)` — historical mouse-handling crash; regression tests here must prove unknown mouse sequences are inert.
- `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` — architecture notes for the worklist input/refresh loop.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** Herdr's terminal supports SGR mouse reporting (1006) — all mainstream terminals do; if not, events simply never arrive (fail-soft, keyboard remains fully usable).
- **Risk — mouse sequences misparsed as keys:** raw chunks like `\x1b[<0;10;5M` must be fully consumed by the mouse path; partial-buffer splits (a chunk split across reads) must be buffered until the terminating `M`/`m`. Mitigated by dedicated parser tests including split-chunk cases.
- **Risk — drag-motion events:** button codes with the 32 motion bit arrive during drags; guard so motion never jumps the selection. Out of scope: implementing drag-to-scroll as a scroll gesture (recorded as a follow-up opportunity rather than expanding scope).
- **Risk — double-click timing:** a ~400 ms window is standard; on slow terminals two intentional clicks may land outside it — acceptable, Enter remains available.
- **Risk — regression to chord/agent shortcuts:** mouse input must not intercept or swallow chord leader keys; the keypress path is unchanged except that mouse-shaped sequences are consumed first.
- **Scope-creep guard:** hover highlighting, drag-to-scroll, right-click context menus, and horizontal touch gestures are NOT in scope; if valuable, they should be captured as linked work items, not added to this item.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MLLGKZ7A1HUL8HU** – Add links to dependencies in the metadata output of the details pane in the TUI. (open)
- **WL-0MSGAEXER000707R** – Pi agent pane opened via a+a (audit) starts in herdr plugin source dir, not the project root (completed)
- **WL-0MNC79G3P004NZXH** – Markdown formatting in Description and Comments field (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH-remove-skill-ralph-directory-tree/skill/intakeall/tests/test_intakeall.py` — matched: events, item, list, make, packages, sensitive, support, touch, work
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH-remove-skill-ralph-directory-tree/command/intake.md` — matched: events, intent, item, list, seed, sensitive, support, work
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH-remove-skill-ralph-directory-tree/docs/workflow/validation-rules.md` — matched: intent, item, list, make, select, selection, support, work


---

## Plan (generated 2026-08-07 by /skill:plan)

**Approach:** Additive mouse/touch support over the existing SGR mouse-reporting protocol, behind the existing raw-mode lifecycle, with a pure-function parser/dispatch design mirroring `handleKeypress` (unit-testable, fail-soft). Decomposed into 4 vertical slices (test-first) + 1 recorded follow-up.

### Features (child work items)

1. **Test: mouse input handling suite** (WL-0MSI720DX002E9WC) — `task`, high. Test-first suite covering all 8 parent ACs: lifecycle sequence emission, SGR parser incl. split chunks, per-mode row mapping, click/double-click/wheel/filter-tap dispatch, drag-motion guard, unknown-sequence inertness, keyboard regression.
2. **Implement: mouse tracking lifecycle + SGR parser** (WL-0MSI7278X0008XGM) — `feature`, medium. ANSI enable/disable constants, emit on raw-mode entry / cleanup, pure `parseMouseEvent` with chunk buffering. Depends on 1.
3. **Implement: mouse dispatch and interactions** (WL-0MSI72EYW00050N2) — `feature`, medium. Row mapping per mode, `mapMouseToAction`, dispatch from `onData` before keypress path, ~400 ms double-click window, wheel/touch scroll (list selection + detail scroll incl. ToC-focus nuance), filter-prompt tap, drag-motion guard. Depends on 1, 2.
4. **Docs, build and verification** (WL-0MSI72L3O005BIW5) — `task`, medium. Update `docs/dev/pause-when-hidden.md` + README notes, rebuild `packages/herdr/dist`, full suite green, manual smoke-run evidence comment. Depends on 3.

### Recorded follow-up (out of scope here, per scope-creep guard)

- **Follow-up: drag-to-scroll in Herdr worklist** (WL-0MSI72S0Y0060BRK) — `feature`, low, sibling with `discovered-from:WL-0MSGHM5BQ0096BNJ`. Drag/touch-drag scroll; must respect the drag-motion guard.

### Assumptions recorded during planning

- A1: Clicks on non-list areas (header, notification row, metadata panel) are inert (ignored safely) — derived from constraints.
- A2: Wheel events in filter mode are ignored (filter options have no arrow-key path today; tap and digit keys are the selectors).
- A3: Wheel in detail mode mirrors j/k semantics, including the detail-ToC-focus nuance (WL-0MSHWHULZ001FL8I): wheel over the ToC moves ToC selection; wheel over the document scrolls it.
- A4: Double-click maps to the Enter-equivalent action for the current mode; exact Enter semantics in detail mode are mirrored as-is (implementer verifies during implementation; this plan captures intent only).
- A5: SGR 1006 is the only required protocol; terminals without it fail soft (keyboard fully usable) — already stated in parent constraints.

# Herdr selection list: metadata section should use the same icons as the list section

## Problem statement

In the herdr work item selection list, the list rows already render icons for
status, stage (audit-aware for `in_review`), producer-review flag, epic type,
and priority. The metadata section (the panel below the list, and the detail
view's metadata table) renders the same fields as **plain text**, so the two
sections are visually inconsistent: users must read words in the metadata panel
where the list shows icons at a glance.

## Users

Herdr plugin users who browse work items via the selection list and read the
selected item's metadata.

- As a user, I want the metadata panel to show the same status/stage/priority
  icons as the list rows so I can scan the selected item's state at a glance.
- As a user, I want icons in the metadata to be accompanied by their text label
  so I never have to guess an icon's meaning.
- As a user who has disabled icons (text-only mode), I want the metadata to fall
  back to plain text labels.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `buildMetaRows` (shared by the list-mode metadata panel and the detail
  view metadata table) prefixes Status, Stage, Priority, Type, Risk, and Effort
  values with the **same icon helpers the list section uses** (`statusIcon`,
  `stageIcon`, `priorityIcon`, `epicIcon`, `riskIcon`, `effortIcon` from
  `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`).
- [ ] The Stage row mirrors the list's audit-aware `in_review` icon logic
  (✅/❌/❓ when fresh, ⏳/⚠️ when stale-but-passed, 🔍 otherwise) via a shared
  helper so list and metadata can never diverge.
- [ ] The Type row shows the epic icon (⊙) for `epic` items only, matching the
  list; non-epic types remain text-only.
- [ ] Icons render as **icon + text label** (e.g. `🔄 in_progress`, `⭐ high`,
  `📥 intake_complete`). When icons are disabled, values render as **text
  only** (no emoji, no bracketed fallbacks like `[HIGH]`).
- [ ] Audit and Reviewed rows also render icon + text labels for consistency
  (e.g. `✅ ready to close`, `❌ needs review`) under the same noIcons rule.
- [ ] Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` cover: icon+text
  values in the metadata panel and detail view, audit-aware stage icon for
  `in_review`, epic icon on Type, text-only fallback when icons are disabled,
  and existing tests are updated for the new value format.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
  (`packages/herdr/README.md` metadata-panel/audit-indicators sections).

## Constraints

- Metadata rows are label/value pairs; the value becomes `icon + text`.
  Truncation must keep working (`truncateLine`), including with multi-cell
  emoji.
- The shared row builder means the list-mode metadata panel and the detail view
  change together (confirmed: both).
- Must honor the existing noIcons/text-fallback convention — but the metadata
  falls back to plain text values, not the bracket labels the list uses.
- No new icons: reuse the existing icon set in `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`.
- The worklog data model is unchanged; this is display-only.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` provides all needed icon helpers (status,
  stage, priority, epic, risk, effort, audit, review) plus an audit-freshness
  check (`isAuditFresh`) and `stringDisplayWidth` for alignment.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` `formatItemLine`/`getIconPrefix` render the
  list rows with icons; `getIconPrefix` inlines the audit-aware stage icon
  logic.
- `buildMetaRows` (worklist.ts) builds the metadata label/value pairs shared by
  `formatMetadataPanel` (list-mode panel) and `formatDetailContent` (detail
  view). Status/Stage/Priority/Type/Risk/Effort are plain text; Audit and
  Reviewed already show icons (icon only, no label).
- `iconsEnabled()` is currently only consulted by the list renderer; the
  metadata/detail paths have no icon toggle today.

## Desired change

1. Extract the audit-aware stage icon selection from `getIconPrefix` into a
   shared exported helper (e.g. `stageDisplayIcon(item, opts)` in icons.ts) and
   use it in both the list prefix and the metadata Stage row.
2. Thread an icon option (e.g. `opts?: IconOptions` / `noIcons`) into
   `buildMetaRows`, `formatMetadataPanel`, `formatDetailContent`, and their call
   sites (list renderer, detail view, metadata-scroll helpers) so the metadata
   honors the same icon toggle as the list.
3. In `buildMetaRows`, render `icon + text` for Status, Stage, Priority, Type
   (epic only), Risk, Effort — plain text when icons are disabled. Add text
   labels to the existing Audit/Reviewed icon rows.
4. Update/extend unit tests and the README.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts` — Extract shared audit-aware stage icon helper; reuse existing icon functions.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `buildMetaRows` icon+text values; thread icon option through `formatMetadataPanel`/`formatDetailContent` and call sites.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — New/updated tests for icon+text metadata, audit-aware stage icon, text-only fallback.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Document icon+text metadata rendering.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** Effort values in the metadata are free-form (e.g. `3`); `effortIcon` returns `''` for unknown keys, so those rows remain text-only — acceptable and consistent with the list.
- **Assumption:** Audit/Reviewed text labels are chosen as `ready to close` / `not ready` / `unknown` and `needs review` / `reviewed`; if the operator prefers different wording, adjust before implementation.
- **Risk (low):** Multi-cell emoji in metadata values could interact with `truncateLine`'s per-code-point counting; mitigated by keeping icons at the value start and existing truncation + `stringDisplayWidth` helpers.
- **Risk (low):** Changing the shared `buildMetaRows` affects the detail view and any tests asserting exact strings; tests will be updated in the same change.
- **Scope-creep guard:** Do not add new icons to the list section or alter the icon set itself — this change only makes the metadata section render the existing icons. Any further icon work (e.g. new statuses, custom type icons) should be tracked as separate work items.

## Related work

- `WL-0MSAYNVBY006LM9X` — Herdr plugin: reserve bottom 40% of selection list for item metadata and last command (created the metadata panel this change targets).
- `WL-0MS6MOXNQ005B9IC` — Metadata in work-item detail views should be presented as markdown table (detail view metadata format).
- `WL-0MS3ALBD40006RGD` — Add audit result display to Herdr plugin detail view (Audit/Reviewed rows).
- `WL-0MQEJ2SLX009X17O` — Add risk and effort T-shirt size icons to Pi TUI work item selection list (same icon language).
- `WL-0MRJ3TUPP002TSGI` — Change in_review icons and reuse audit column for requiresProducerReview flag (list icon behavior this change mirrors).
- `WL-0MP160TK9001WPVQ` — Implement icons in TUI detail pane (main-project counterpart; open, related-to).

## Related work (automated report)

> Automated artifact from `/skill:find-related WL-0MSGIXHHI009KFW9`. The matches below are low-relevance keyword hits (generic terms such as "item", "list", "status"); the manual Related work section above carries the actionable links.

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRFOJFVA003S8IB** – Compact footer status line: shorten skill indicator and truncate work item IDs (completed)
- **WL-0MQJK4UGN000CHUF** – Split src/github.ts into domain-specific modules (completed)
- **WL-0MKXMGIQ90NU8UQB** – Workflow (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH-remove-skill-ralph-directory-tree/AGENTS.md` — matched: display, effort, epic, item, list, priority, risk, section, should, stage, status, type, use, used, work
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH-remove-skill-ralph-directory-tree/skill/plan/SKILL.md` — matched: display, effort, epic, item, list, priority, risk, section, should, stage, status, type, use, used, work
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: display, effort, epic, item, list, priority, risk, section, should, stage, status, type, use, used, work

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Scope — `buildMetaRows` is shared between the list-mode metadata panel and the detail view. Should the icons appear in both, or only in the list-mode metadata panel?" — Answer (operator): "both". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "The list shows an audit-aware icon for `in_review` stage (✅/❌/❓/⏳/⚠️); the metadata already has a separate Audit row. Should the Stage row mirror the list's audit-aware icon, or use the plain stage icon (🔍)?" — Answer (operator): "yes" (mirror the list's audit-aware icon). Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Should the metadata icons respect the no-icons/text-fallback mode, or always render emoji?" — Answer (operator): "in the meta-data we should render both if possible, fallback to text only" (icon + text label when icons are enabled; plain text only when disabled). Source: interactive reply.

# Herdr selection list: shortcut hint bar empty until a chord key is pressed

## Problem statement

In the Herdr "Worklog Selection List" pane (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`), the footer hint bar that shows the available shortcut commands (e.g. `c:create new  i:implement  u:update...  x:close...`) is empty when the list opens. The hints only appear after the user presses the first key of a chord (e.g. `u`), at which point a `chord: u _ ...` footer renders. The behavior is inconsistent: the initial hints are gated behind the `showHelpText` plugin setting, but the chord-in-progress footer is not gated by it.

## Users

Herdr users who run the Worklog Selection List pane and rely on the footer hint bar to discover keyboard shortcuts.

- As a user opening the Worklog Selection List, I want to see the available shortcut commands in the hint bar immediately, so I know which keys are available without pressing them first.
- As a user who has deliberately disabled help text, I want the setting to behave consistently (all hint lines hidden, including chord-mode hints), matching the pi browse widget.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. With `showHelpText` on (the default), the footer hint bar shows the available shortcut commands as soon as the selection list opens — before any chord key is pressed. (No change to the current on-state rendering.)
2. With `showHelpText` off, the chord-in-progress footer (`chord: <keys> _ <hints>`) is also hidden, so no shortcut hints render in any mode — consistent with the pi browse widget's `showHelpText` handling.
3. The `showHelpText` default remains `true` in `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` (`defaultSettings`), `loadSettings()` fallback, and `runWorklistTui` options; verify no code path silently defaults it to `false`.
4. The user's local Herdr config (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`) is set so `showHelpText` is `true` (or the key is removed to fall back to the default), restoring the visible hint bar for the reporter.
5. Automated tests cover: (a) chord-mode footer suppressed when `showHelpText` is `false`, and (b) chord-mode footer present when `showHelpText` is `true`/unset. Full project test suite passes.
6. Documentation is updated to reflect the change: the Herdr README's `showHelpText` description (`packages/herdr/README.md`) accurately states that `false` hides all shortcut hint lines, including chord-mode hints; code comments on the renderer footer and call site explain the gating.

## Constraints

- Keep the `showHelpText` setting; do not remove or repurpose it (operator decision C).
- The Herdr plugin reads settings from `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` (via `loadSettings()`); the repo must not depend on the reporter's local config for tests.
- The chord key *handling* (state machine) must keep working even when the hint footer is hidden — only rendering is affected.
- Backward compatibility for `createListRenderer` callers: adding a renderer parameter must not break existing tests that call it positionally.

## Existing state

- The initial shortcut hints are computed as `dynamicHints` in `runWorklistTui` and passed to the renderer only when `opts.getShowHelpText()` is true (`worklist.ts` ~line 2666: `opts.getShowHelpText() ? dynamicHints : undefined`).
- The renderer footer (`createListRenderer`, `worklist.ts` ~lines 1683–1697) has two branches:
  - chord active (`chordState.pendingKeys.length > 0`): always renders `chord: <keys> _ <hints>` using `chordState.hints` — **not** gated by `showHelpText`.
  - otherwise: renders `[esc] back` nav hint plus `chordHelpHints` — gated by `showHelpText` at the call site.
- With the reporter's config `showHelpText: false` this yields: empty footer on open; `chord: u _ update...` footer once a chord key is pressed — exactly the reported behavior.
- The pi browse widget (`packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/lib/browse.ts`) gates the entire help line (including chord hints `🔗 …`) behind `currentSettings.showHelpText` — consistent, and the reference behavior for this fix.
- The reporter's local config `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` currently contains `"showHelpText": false`.

## Desired change

1. Gate the chord-in-progress footer in the renderer behind `showHelpText` so `showHelpText: false` hides all hint lines (normal and chord-mode), matching the pi widget.
   - Suggested approach: add a trailing `showHelpText` parameter to `createListRenderer`'s returned renderer (defaulting to `true` when `undefined`, preserving existing positional callers/tests), render the chord footer only when `isChordActive && showHelpText`, and pass `opts.getShowHelpText()` from `runWorklistTui`'s call site.
2. Add/extend renderer tests covering the chord-footer gating above (see AC 5).
3. Update the reporter's local `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` so `showHelpText` is `true` (or remove the key), restoring the visible hint bar.

## Risks & assumptions

- The chosen behavior (C) means users with `showHelpText: false` get **no** visual chord feedback at all (not even `chord: u _`). This matches the pi widget but is a UX tradeoff — documented in the README update (AC 6).
- Chord key *handling* must keep working with the footer hidden; the fix must only affect rendering. Guard with a test that chord state still accumulates while `showHelpText` is `false`.
- Adding a trailing `showHelpText` param to `createListRenderer` must not break existing positional callers/tests (default `true` when `undefined`).
- The reporter's local config fix (`~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json`) is out-of-repo; the implementing agent cannot commit it — it must be applied locally (AC 4) or the key removed to use the default.
- Scope-creep guard: adjacent renderer/footer improvements (e.g., "items below the fold" — WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ) are separate work items; do not expand scope.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — `createListRenderer` footer branch: gate chord-mode footer behind `showHelpText`; `runWorklistTui` call site: pass `opts.getShowHelpText()` to the renderer.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — new tests: chord footer hidden when `showHelpText: false`; chord footer shown when `true`/unset.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — verification only: confirm `showHelpText` default stays `true`.
- `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` — local (out-of-repo) change: set `showHelpText` to `true`.

## Related work

- `WL-0MS4FJ2TX009V7V5` — "Rich settings: browseItemCount and showHelpText toggle" (completed): introduced the `showHelpText` setting for Herdr; commit `d637c9b2` gated the initial help hints but left the chord footer ungated — the root of this inconsistency.
- `WL-0MS3ANM1H007SG92` — "Rich settings for Herdr plugin: browseItemCount and showHelpText" (completed): companion/parent settings work.
- `WL-0MS31Q7FD00710B7` — "Chord shortcut system & dynamic help bar" (completed): the chord system + help bar this issue touches.
- `WL-0MQEBM6OM004Q1Q7` — "Chord dispatch and help text in browse views" (completed): chord/help-text behavior in the pi browse views (the consistency reference).
- `WL-0MSG8YXYJ008PWJJ` — "Herdr selection list: no indication of items below the fold" (open): separate issue on the same renderer/component (`createListRenderer`); may touch adjacent footer/list-area code.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What should the desired end state be? A) hint bar always shows regardless of `showHelpText` (remove/repurpose the setting); B) keep the setting and set the config to `true`; C) keep the setting and fix the inconsistency — `showHelpText` off hides *all* hints including chord-mode ones (consistent with the pi widget)."
  - Answer (operator): "C — on by default." Source: interactive reply.
  - Interpretation: keep the `showHelpText` setting; gate the chord-mode footer behind it so `false` hides all hint lines; the setting default must remain `true` (it already is in `settings.ts` `defaultSettings`, `loadSettings()` fallback, and `runWorklistTui` options — verification-only AC 3). The reporter's local config currently overrides the default to `false`, so it must be flipped to `true` (or the key removed) for the hint bar to be visible again (AC 4).
  - Note: chord key *handling* must remain functional with the footer hidden; only rendering is affected.

# Show plugin version in Herdr work item selection list (WL-0MSGKEBFU004T3N3)

## Problem statement

The Herdr Worklog work item selection list gives no indication of which plugin version is running, making it hard to verify installs, spot stale builds, or report bugs accurately. A dimmed, right-aligned version number in the pane header solves this without visual clutter.

## Users

- **Herdr users** who want to confirm which version of the Worklog Selection List plugin is running.
- **Developers/support** who need the version handy when filing bug reports or verifying an updated build is live.

### User stories

- As a Herdr user, I want to see the plugin version in the corner of the work item list, so I can confirm which build I'm running.
- As a developer, I want the version visible but unobtrusive, so it doesn't distract from the list content.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The work item selection list header shows the plugin version (`0.1.0` from `packages/herdr/package.json`), right-aligned to the pane width.
2. The version is rendered in the dimmed ANSI style (`\x1b[2m`), matching the existing `[auto-refresh on]` treatment, and does not interfere with the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title.
3. The version is read at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` (not hardcoded in the renderer), so it stays in sync with the manifest version.
4. Unit tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` cover the header rendering with the version suffix, including a case without a version available (graceful fallback).
5. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Unobtrusive: dimmed font, right-aligned to the pane edge; must not change existing header content or alignment of the title.
- Use existing patterns: `termSize.cols` for pane width, `ANSI.dim` for dimming, `readFileSync` for reading `package.json` (pattern already used in `worklist.ts`/`shortcut-config.ts`).
- No changes to `herdr-plugin.toml` version unless a version bump is explicitly requested.
- Do not update CHANGELOG.md (managed automatically by the ship skill release pipeline).

## Existing state

- The selection list header is rendered in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (~line 1585): ` Work Items — N item(s)` plus optional `[auto-refresh on]` (dimmed) and `[paused — hidden]` indicators.
- `termSize` (with `cols`) is available in the render function; `truncateLine()` handles width overflow.
- The plugin version is declared in two places: `packages/herdr/package.json` (`"version": "0.1.0"`) and `packages/herdr/herdr-plugin.toml` (`version = "0.1.0"`). There is currently no runtime version constant.
- Existing header tests in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` (lines ~86–100) assert `'Work Items'` presence.

## Desired change

1. Add a runtime helper that reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (e.g., parse JSON, fall back to a safe default like `'?'` or omit when unreadable).
2. In the list-mode header renderer, append a dimmed `v<version>` string right-aligned to `cols` (using padding), while keeping the title left-aligned.
3. Add unit tests covering: version suffix present and right-aligned, dim style applied, graceful fallback when the version can't be read.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — Header rendering; add version read + right-aligned dimmed suffix (near line 1585).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — Header assertions for version suffix, alignment, and fallback.
- `packages/herdr/package.json` — Version source (`0.1.0`); no change expected.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Optional: document the version display.

## Related work

- **WL-0MS1W8Y1L0059AKP** — Create a work item selection list in Herdr: parent feature that produced `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`.
- **WL-0MQHYI4E60075SQT** — Fix icon prefix alignment in Pi TUI work item selection list: related header/line formatting work (Pi TUI counterpart).
- **WL-0MSBVS4AS006ZQEZ** — Herdr selection list refreshes immediately when its tab regains focus: related Herdr list behavior work.
- **WL-0MQL0T5TR0060AEH** — Add activity-indicator footer to Worklog Pi extension: related footer/status UI precedent (Pi TUI counterpart).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKX5ZV3D0OHIIX2** – Add regression tests for mouse click crash and TUI behavior (completed)
- **WL-0MKZ34IDI0XTA5TB** – TUI: Reparent items without typing IDs (completed)
- **WL-0MQL0T5TR0060AEH** – Add activity-indicator footer to Worklog Pi extension (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MS1T7A5W003UJUH-remove-skill-ralph-directory-tree/tests/test_ralph_loop.py` — matched: add, item, list, number, position, show, src, using, version, work
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSGKAWXQ009VVG2-enforce-git-worktree-usage-for-all-imple/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: add, item, list, number, position, show, using, version, work
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: add, item, list, number, position, show, using, version, work

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: `package.json` is present next to the compiled/tsx module at runtime; the module-dir relative read pattern (as in `shortcut-config.ts`) works for both `npx tsx` and `dist` runs.
- **Risk**: ANSI codes in a right-padded line can misalign padding calculations if padding is computed on raw text length; must compute visible-width padding before applying ANSI styles.
- **Risk**: Very narrow panes could crowd the header; the version suffix should be dropped or truncated if it would overlap the title (guard on `cols`).
- **Scope creep risk**: Bumping the version, adding the version elsewhere (footer/status bar), or showing `wl`/ContextHub versions — out of scope; record as follow-up work items if desired.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1**: "Which version number? I assume the plugin's own version (`0.1.0` from `packages/herdr/package.json` / `herdr-plugin.toml`) — or did you mean the `wl` CLI version or ContextHub's version?"  
  **Answer** (user): "yes the plugins" — the Worklog Selection List plugin's own version. Source: interactive reply.

- **Q2**: "Placement preference? Unobtrusive, dimmed — candidates: (a) right side of the header line, (b) footer hint line, (c) bottom-right corner."  
  **Answer** (user): "a (right aligned to width of pane)" — right-aligned in the header line. Source: interactive reply.

# Intake Brief — Insert selected work-item ID into herdr command input forms (WL-0MSGPSEFW006VINF)

## Problem statement

When typing a free-form prompt in a herdr command input form (e.g. the `P-p` chord, which opens a prompt sent to a new Pi agent pane), there is no discoverable way to reference the currently selected work item by its ID. The `<id>` magic token already works inside form field values (both chord and single-key form paths in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` resolve it to the selected item's ID on submit), but the behavior is undocumented, untested, and invisible in the UI — and in one edge case (no item selected, `P-p` path) a literal `<id>` leaks through to Pi.

## Users

- **Herdr users** who open the `P-p` free-form prompt (or any chord form) and want the prompt to reference the work item they currently have selected — without memorising/pasting the ID.
- **Pi agents / operators** who receive the prompt — the prompt becomes self-contained with the item ID, so no follow-up lookup is needed.

User stories:
- As a Herdr user with an item selected in the worklist, I want to type `<id>` in the `P-p` free-form prompt so the selected item's ID is inserted into the prompt sent to Pi.
- As a Herdr user filling any chord command form (e.g. `u-t` title, `u-s` stage), I want `<id>` to resolve to the currently selected item's ID the same way it does in command templates.
- As a new Herdr user, I want the form dialog to hint that `<id>` is available, so I don't need to read the README to discover it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Typing `<id>` in the `P-p` free-form prompt field inserts the currently selected work item's ID into the prompt text sent to Pi (verified by an automated regression test on the form-submit path; no new `wl` spawn needed).
2. The same `<id>`-in-field behavior works in **all** herdr command input forms, for both the chord and single-key dispatch paths.
3. The form dialog renders a discoverability hint (e.g. a footer/help line such as "type `<id>` to insert the selected item's ID") whenever the form is shown.
4. When no work item is selected and a form field value contains `<id>`, the behavior is graceful and consistent across all paths — no literal `<id>` is sent to Pi; the documented decision (see Risks & assumptions) is implemented and covered by a test.
5. `packages/herdr/README.md` documents the `<id>`-in-form-field behavior, including the `P-p` free-prompt example.
6. Full project test suite passes with the new changes; new tests cover the free-prompt case, the generic form case, the no-item-selected edge case, and the discoverability hint.

## Constraints

- **No change to `<id>` handling in command templates** — the existing `KNOWN_IDENTIFIERS` / `substituteIdentifiers` mechanism in `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` stays as-is.
- **No changes to the chord definitions** in `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json` (P-p, P-a, u-*, etc. remain bound exactly as today).
- No modal/UX overhaul of the form dialog — the hint is a minimal addition to the existing form render.
- All work tracked in wl; no changes to work-item tracking tooling.

## Existing state

- `P-p` chord → `/prompt:<prompt>` opens the command input form (`FormState` in `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts`); on submit the resulting command routes through `worklist.ts` and spawns a Pi agent pane with the bare prompt text (`stripAgentPromptPrefix` in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`).
- `KNOWN_IDENTIFIERS = {'id'}` in `form-dialog.ts` — `<id>` never triggers an unknown-identifier prompt; `substituteIdentifiers` leaves `<id>` intact in field values.
- Both form onSubmit callbacks in `worklist.ts` (chord-complete path ~line 2353 and single-key path ~line 2464) replace `<id>` with the selected item's ID via `flat[idx].id`.
- No regression test covers `<id>` typed inside a form field value; no UI hint; README documents `<id>` resolution for command templates only, not for field values/free prompts.
- Edge case: in the form paths, when no item is selected and the field value contains `<id>`, `finalCmd` keeps the literal `<id>` and it is sent (visible to Pi in the `P-p` case); the non-form `executeResolvedCommand` path instead returns a graceful `noop` when `<id>` is in the command and nothing is selected — inconsistent.

## Desired change

- **Verify + formalise the existing mechanism**: add regression tests asserting `<id>` in a form field value resolves to the selected item's ID, for the free prompt (P-p) and generic forms, across chord and single-key paths.
- **Discoverability**: render a hint line in the form dialog ("type `<id>` to insert the selected item's ID") and document the behavior in `packages/herdr/README.md` (including the `P-p` free-prompt example).
- **Graceful no-item-selected handling**: decide and implement one consistent behavior for `<id>` in field values when nothing is selected (proposed: drop the command with a toast, matching the existing `noop` convention for template `<id>`; documented in the work item).
- **No new mechanism** — the magic-token approach was chosen in intake (option a); chord-based insertion and pre-filled prompts were considered and explicitly out of scope.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.ts` — render the `<id>` discoverability hint in the form dialog (footer/help line); unchanged substitution logic.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — the two form onSubmit callbacks: consistent no-item-selected handling (drop + toast); no change to existing `<id>` resolution.
- `packages/herdr/src/form-dialog.test.ts`, `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — regression tests for `<id>`-in-field resolution, the no-item-selected edge case, and the hint rendering.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — document `<id>` inside form field values / free prompts.

## Related work

- **Herdr shortcuts: P-p free prompt and P-a audit-gaps prompt (WL-0MSGHNTMF000YKRI)** — completed; introduced the `P-p` chord this feature builds on.
- **Herdr plugin: free-form prompt shortcut opens new pi pane (WL-0MSC0O8HN000EBFH)** — completed; `/prompt:` routing + `send-to-pi.sh` pane spawning.
- **Form input dialog for unknown identifiers in Herdr chord commands (WL-0MS690SJG003H7WK)** — completed; introduced `FormState` / form-dialog.
- **Shortcuts with multiple <id> tokens only replace the first occurrence (WL-0MRNLF5UO0088ID2)** — completed; multiple-`<id>` handling relevant to the `u-t`/`u-s` edge case.
- **Wire text-insertion template commands (WL-0MS4GIMBD008GWVM)** — completed; text-insertion template wiring in the same code area.
- **Related work (automated report, /skill:find-related)** — additional matches retained as lower-priority context: **wl sync timeouts (WL-0MSAKM838006RZNR)** (completed; herdr auto-sync spawn/timeout context), **[test-failure] send-to-pi.sh / open-pi-agent.sh pane-launch tests (WL-0MSGAKL8R009GB1X)** (completed; pane-launch regression relevant to the P-p spawn path), **Unify dialog widget construction and layout helpers (WL-0MNX4D4G8009XZNJ)** (completed; form-dialog rendering helpers). Automated repo-file matches (audit_runner.py, intake SKILL.md) were reviewed and dropped — generic keyword noise from the wrong repo root.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Over-implementation risk:** the mechanism already exists; the main risk is building a redundant insertion mechanism instead of testing + surfacing the existing magic token. Mitigation: scope is verification, discoverability, and edge-case handling only.
- **No-item-selected edge case:** proposed default = drop the command with a toast (consistent with template `<id>` noop convention). Assumption: users prefer a clear "no item selected" signal over sending a literal `<id>` to Pi.
- **Multi-`<id>` forms (`u-t` title, `u-s` stage):** typing `<id>` into such a field replaces every `<id>` in the command (target and field value) with the selected ID — existing multiple-`<id>` behavior, accepted as-is; noted in docs.
- **Scope-creep risk:** chord-based insertion and pre-filled prompts (intake options b/c) are out of scope; if requested later, record as linked work items rather than expanding this one.
- **Assumption:** the selected item is the one highlighted in the herdr worklist (`state.selectedIndex`), same source used by all existing `<id>` substitutions.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "The `WL-0MSAZQEQB008O7H3` reference — that ID is an existing, unrelated in-progress work item (the wl read-cache epic). Which did you mean? (a) It was simply the item currently selected in your herdr pane — the feature is generic: insert *whatever* item is currently selected. (b) It should be a magic token: typing that literal string into the prompt gets replaced with the currently selected item's ID before sending. (c) Something else." — Answer (operator): "a" — generic; insert whatever item is currently selected. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Insertion mechanism — how should the ID get into the input box while typing? (a) A magic token in the prompt text (e.g. typing `<id>` — consistent with the existing placeholder convention in herdr commands). (b) A chord/keypress *inside* the input box (e.g. a key or chord that pastes the selected ID at the cursor). (c) Open the P-p prompt pre-filled with the selected ID. (d) Freeform." — Answer (operator): "a" — magic token (`<id>`). Source: interactive reply. Note: (b) and (c) explicitly out of scope.
- Q3: "Scope — which input boxes should support this? (a) Only the herdr P-p free-prompt input box. (b) All herdr command input forms. (c) Also the main pi prompt input (the `P` key in the pi TUI) — note: that lives in pi core and may not be reachable from a herdr plugin extension." — Answer (operator): "b" — all herdr command input forms. Source: interactive reply. Note: pi core input out of scope.
- Q4 (agent research note, no user answer required): does typing `<id>` in a form field already work? — Research: inspected `form-dialog.ts` (`KNOWN_IDENTIFIERS`, `substituteIdentifiers`) and both onSubmit callbacks in `worklist.ts`; the mechanism already resolves `<id>` to the selected item's ID on submit in both chord and single-key paths. No test covers this path; no UI hint; `P-p` with no item selected leaks literal `<id>` to Pi. Findings incorporated into Existing state / Desired change.

## Summary

`wl next` (and `wl next -n <count>`) currently returns items whose stage is `done`, wasting fetch budget and polluting top-N work lists. Verified: `wl next -n 20 --include-in-progress` returned 20 items of which **12 had stage=done** (e.g. WL-0MMKENAJT14229DE, WL-0MMTDALZO0KQEZMI). Downstream consumers (herdr worklist `fetchNextItems`, pi TUI) then must filter them out client-side, and the TUI fetch budget is effectively reduced (herdr showed 9 items instead of 20 because 12 of the fetched 20 were done).

## User story

As an operator using wl next or a TUI that consumes it, I want done items excluded from results so that the top-N list is full of actionable work and no downstream filtering is needed.

## Expected behaviour

- `wl next` returns only non-done items by default (stage not in [done]).
- `wl next -n 20` returns up to 20 actionable items.
- The `--stage done` filter still allows explicitly requesting done items (filter semantics unchanged: stage filters remain explicit opt-in).
- Existing behaviour for other stages/statuses unchanged; dependency-blocked and in-progress handling unchanged.

## Implementation notes

- Likely in the `next` command implementation (src/commands/next.ts in ContextHub, which is also the global worklog CLI via npm link).
- Add an exclusion predicate for stage=done in the default (unfiltered) query path, similar to how status filters are applied.
- Check existing tests (tests/commands/next.test.ts or similar) and add coverage: a done item is excluded by default, included with explicit --stage done.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `wl next -n 20 --include-in-progress` returns zero items with stage=done.
- [ ] `wl next --stage done -n 5` still returns done items.
- [ ] All existing tests pass; new tests cover the exclusion and the explicit --stage done opt-in.
- [ ] herdr worklist pane no longer needs its client-side stage=done filter (may be kept as defensive).
